title: Shot accordion scratchpad
content:
Purpose
- quick personal notebook for trying the "shot accordion" idea: dynamically compressing/expanding few-shot exemplars depending on token budget and cue strength.
- capture failure modes, small exemplar banks, and heuristics to pick N and ordering.

Core idea (working phrasing)
- For a given instruction, maintain a compact ranked bank of exemplars (E1..Ek). At request time choose an accordion factor a in [0,1] that controls how many exemplars or how verbose each exemplar should be included. High a => include more full exemplars; low a => include tiny labels or single-line hints.
- Rationale: some tasks need rich context to avoid hallucination; others are brittle to exemplar noise and need only one archetype. Avoid static N.

Quick heuristics to try (priority order)
1) Start with a = clamp(0.25 + 0.5 * cue_confidence, 0,1) where cue_confidence is a lightweight similarity score between user prompt and exemplar cluster centroids.
2) If expected tokens > budget -> reduce exemplar verbosity first, then reduce exemplar count.
3) If last response had >2 hallucinatory facts (post-hoc), increase a by +0.15 next attempt.
4) Prefer exemplars with same output format markers (JSON / YAML / bullet list) when formatting strictness tag present.

Exemplar bank (mini set for intent-class: "extract consequences")
- E1 (full): "Instruction: List concrete downstream consequences. Input: A startup folds after Series A. Output: 1) Customers lose support..." (3 short bullets)
- E2 (compact): "Label: consequences-of-failure -> loss of customers, layoffs, long-term brand damage"
- E3 (micro): "Pattern: cause -> effect -> timeframe"

Few-shot template variants to try
- Verbose block (N=3 full): 
  [SYSTEM] You are a concise analyst.
  [EX1] ...full exemplar...
  [EX2] ...full exemplar...
  [INPUT] {user_input}
  [OUTPUT]
- Accordion compressed (a=0.4): 
  [SYSTEM] You are a concise analyst.
  [EX1] Label + 1-sentence hint
  [EX2] micro-pattern only
  [INPUT] {user_input}
  [OUTPUT]
- Label-only baseline (a~0):
  [SYSTEM] You are a concise analyst.
  [EX] Label tokens ("consequence-skeleton")
  [INPUT] {user_input}
  [OUTPUT]

Failure cases observed (notes from quick runs)
- When exemplars contain dated facts (2019-specific), model hallucinates timeline details; compression did not help because label-to-fact mapping leaked in few tokens.
- Over-compressing (a < 0.2) led to format drift: model outputs paragraphs instead of bullets even when an exemplar format marker present.
- Similarity heuristic sometimes picks near-duplicate exemplars that bias style; need diversity penalty.

Small experiments to run (1-2 token budgets + quality metric)
- Matrix: {budget: 256, 512, 1024} x {a: 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} x {similarity: tf-idf, SBERT}
- Metrics: format_accuracy (exact match on bullet structure), hallucination_rate (manual label), ROUGE-L to reference if available, latency avg.
- Quick AB test: pick 30 prompts from "customer-impact" cluster; compare a=0.25 vs a=0.75 under budget=512.

Heuristic refinements to implement
- Diversity penalty: pick exemplars by maximizing (similarity_to_query - 0.6 * similarity_to_selected). Simple greedy selection.
- Exemplar verbosity tiers: full / one-liner / label / pattern. Allow per-exemplar override flag.
- Format lock: inject "OUTPUT MUST BE in <format>" as a soft anchor if format_accuracy drops below threshold.

Notes on operationalizing in prompt library
- Store exemplars with metadata: tags, format, exemplar_tier, centroid_embedding, last_used_ts, failure_count. (Implementation: small DB table)
- Provide an API: GET /exemplars?intent=consequence&budget=512&format=bullets -> returns ordered list with suggested tiers and token_cost_estimate.
- Client-side: compute cue_confidence cheaply (approx dot between small embedding) before server-side allocation.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to automatically label exemplar tiers? Heuristic: measure token length + number of sentences + presence of explicit markers. Need to test.
- Should slow re-ranking use full-similarity if budget high? yes but needs caching.
- Cold start: for new intent, fallback to label-only + 1 generic exemplar. Might be safer than multiple noisy exemplars.

Mini checklist for next session
- [ ] implement diversity penalty prototype in notebook 
- [ ] run AB on 30 prompts (a=0.25 vs a=0.75) budget=512
- [ ] add simple token estimator function and integrate exemplar tiers
- [ ] capture 20 failure excerpts and tag them with failure type

Scratch examples (quick)
- User: "What are immediate legal risks if a consumer app leaks user emails?"
  Verbose exemplar output should be bullets with legal sections (data breach, notification laws, fines).
  Compressed label-only: "legal-risks -> breach-notice, fines, litigation, reputation" (Observe: compressed still prompted model to enumerate but sometimes mixed order.)

Last thought (brain dump)
- This could pair well with Redwood Optimize: use historical token-cost vs quality curves to pick a per-customer default 'a' value. Also useful for Dedicated customers who have strict token budgets.

End of scratchpad.
